questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Well, I really liked the Italian culture beforehand, so I wanted to do my exchange in Italy. Also, I had never visited Bologna so it made a lot of sense to go there. Additionally, being located in the middle of Northern Italy, Bologna is a great point of departure for exploring. And then of course the food, the drinks, the football...

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was all right. You can find most information on the website, and if in doubt, you are assigned an instructor who will help you. The bureaucracy of the university is a whole lot more loose in Italy, which you will have to get accustomed to.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a few mails from both KU and the university of Bologna with guidance which was sufficient.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a friend going on exchange in Bologna a year before me, and she knew a "landlord" that I could reach out to. Therefore, for me, it was rather easy to find accommodation. But, in general, accommodation is really difficult in Bologna, and a lot of my friends struggled finding a place to live. Some arrived at Bologna without having acquired accommodation beforehand, and they had a hard to find anything. So, I would recommend finding accommodation as early as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bologna University offers very little accommodation. I lived in an apartment with six other exchange students, so you are not completely cut off of 'the university experience' living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process is pretty much just getting your courses pre-approved at Bologna University, just as you have to do it at KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I found information on the website and then contacted my instructor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite satisfied. Some of the classes I wanted were scheduled at the same time, so obviously I could not follow both. But other than that it was just fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If in doubt, contact your instructor. Besides, look at the website for information.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Even though I was a BA student, most of the classes I followed were second degree programs. But I did not think about it much. I did not find the classes particularity difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes contained much fewer students at Bologna University compared to KU. Therefore, there was much more interaction among the students during the lessons opposed to merely a professor giving a lecture. At Bologna University in general, the professors appreciate active participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Humanitarian Communication
Web Society and Globalization
Urban Studies and Climate Change
Visualizing the Italian Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Humanitarian Communication was definitely my favorite of the four. I will recommend everybody to follow that course. Urban Studies and Climate Change and Visualizing the Italian Society are pretty easy to get by, but not well taught either. Web Society and Globalization is quite interesting, but, for me, yield of the class was too narrow.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected cost, but it is quite expensive being on exchange as you want to use money all the time - whether on food, on drinks, on clothes, on experiences...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going to restaurants is a lot cheaper compared to Denmark. Much of the time, it is not more expensive to eat out than cooking food yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in these, but there are a group of 'Erasmus tutors' who plan a lot of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in these.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around Northern Italy. Go to Venice, Florence, Milano...

Also, just have a good and easy time in Bologna - the city is very laid back.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was all right. I was told beforehand that most Italians are reluctant to speak English, but this is not true.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Many of the classes at the university include group work. Here, the professors appreciate when local students and exchange students work together, and I think it is a good opportunity to getting to know the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I missed rye bread a lot. Also, they eat dinner very late in the evening, which is hard getting accustomed to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I was surprised by Italians' openness. Everyone down in Bologna is very kind. Also, 1/4 of the population are university students. Therefore, there are a lot of young people - and they very modern and cool as well!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get accommodation beforehand - and as early as possible
If you have the time, explore other parts of Italy is well - Bologna's location is key
Go to local places and act like a local 8)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The professors might get a little mad if you call them by their name instead of calling them 'professor'.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being away from family and friends for a long time - in a good way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Again, being away from family and friends, and, as such, being forced to seek new relations and make new habits

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
